root_cause.text: In tpm_dev_release(), the function used plain kfree() instead of kfree_sensitive() to free the authentication session structure (chip->auth), leaving sensitive cryptographic material (HMAC session keys, nonces, passphrase) unscrubbed in freed slab memory, creating an information disclosure vulnerability.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff changes `kfree(chip->auth)` to `kfree_sensitive(chip->auth)` in tpm_dev_release(). The commit message explains that other code paths (tpm2_end_auth_session, tpm_buf_check_hmac_response) already use kfree_sensitive for the same structure, and that chip->auth contains sensitive data such as HMAC session keys, nonces, and passphrase data. This inconsistency is the root cause of the vulnerability.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace kfree with kfree_sensitive for chip->auth to zero sensitive authentication data before freeing, preventing potential information leaks.
intent_record.what: Replaced kfree(chip->auth) with kfree_sensitive(chip->auth) inside the #ifdef CONFIG_TCG_TPM2_HMAC block in the tpm_dev_release function.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when the TPM device is released, the memory pointed to by chip->auth is now zeroed before being freed, ensuring that any sensitive authentication data (e.g., HMAC keys) does not remain in memory after deallocation.
